items.title: Overnight Blaze Destroys a Flatbed Tow Truck Near Pearson in Mississauga's Latest Suspicious Fire
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel police are investigating after an overnight fire destroyed a flatbed tow truck in the area of Dixie Road and Shawson Drive, in Mississauga's east end just west of Toronto Pearson Airport. Police describe the blaze, which broke out early Thursday morning, as suspicious and say it is the latest in a string of similar tow truck fires across the region. According to police, no injuries were reported as a result of the fire. Investigators say they have no information yet on a suspect or suspects. Peel police are asking anyone with information about the incident, including CCTV or dash camera footage, to contact the force's 12 Division Criminal Investigation Bureau. INsauga notes the blaze follows a similar incident on August 6, when a tow truck caught fire while parked in a driveway near Creditview Road and Sandalwood Parkway in Brampton, part of a broader pattern of tow truck fires seen across Mississauga, Brampton and the wider GTA this year and in past years.

items.title: Mississauga Pilots a 40-Appointment Home-Voting Program for Residents Who Can't Leave the House
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, the city is launching a new Vote From Front Door program for the 2026 municipal election to help homebound residents who cannot travel to a voting location and cannot appoint a proxy to vote on their behalf. The program lets eligible residents arrange a scheduled home visit, during which trained election officials walk them through the voting process in person. The city says it is running the program as a pilot, with availability limited to just 40 appointments. According to the city, its Elections Office will review each application individually and make the final call on eligibility. Residents interested in participating can complete an online Vote From Front Door registration form to apply. Approved applicants will receive appointment details and further instructions from the Elections Office ahead of their scheduled voting appointment, the city says. Because only 40 spots are available, the city is encouraging eligible residents to apply as soon as possible.

items.title: City Walks First-Time Voters Through What to Expect Before Mississauga's October 26 Election Day
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, casting a ballot for the first time can feel intimidating, so the city has put together guidance for first-time voters ahead of the municipal election on October 26. The city says voting is also a chance for new voters to help shape decisions that affect daily life in Mississauga, from transit and parks to housing and how the city grows in the years ahead. According to the city, preparation should start before heading to a voting location, including researching the candidates running in a resident's ward and thinking through which issues matter most to them. The city advises voters to confirm where they are supposed to vote and to bring acceptable identification with them on Election Day. Residents who received a voter notification card in the mail are encouraged to bring it along as well, according to the city. The city frames the overall process as more straightforward than many first-time voters expect once they know what to bring and where to go.
